{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABagqK6Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhEHGtY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 63, "title": "Simulate Gamepad haptics for Quest controllers with DevTools visual feedback", "body": "## Problem

The emulated Meta Quest 3 Touch Plus controllers expose `XRInputSource.gamepad` with buttons, axes, connection state and input-source lifetime, but their Gamepads currently have `vibrationActuator: null` and `hapticActuators: []`. WebXR applications that use Gamepad haptics (for example, feedback when grabbing or selecting an object) cannot exercise or inspect their vibration requests on the desktop emulator.

We do **not** need actual controller vibration, native XR hardware integration or a new WebXR feature descriptor. The practical requirement is that the application can call a supported Gamepad haptic operation and the **WebXR DevTools panel visibly shows which virtual controller received what request**. The virtual effect should complete or be canceled with a predictable Promise result and correct source/session lifetime.

## Expected outcome

Add useful, deterministic, entirely simulated haptic output for **both Quest 3 tracked controllers** in **immersive-vr** and **immersive-ar (MR)**. Expose a stable, usable Gamepad haptic actuator through each active `XRInputSource.gamepad`, with a visually observable indication in the existing DevTools panel (e.g. independent left/right controller glow plus intensity/duration readout or a short effect timeline).

Primary API target:

```js
// From an active Quest XRInputSource, not navigator.getGamepads().
const actuator = inputSource.gamepad.vibrationActuator;
const outcome = await actuator.playEffect('dual-rumble', {
  startDelay: 0,
  duration: 250,
  strongMagnitude: 0.8,
  weakMagnitude: 0.4
}); // 'complete' or 'preempted'
await actuator.reset();
```

Use the current [Gamepad API specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/gamepad/#gamepadhapticactuator-interface) and [WebXR Gamepads Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-gamepads-module-1/) to define supported behavior. Haptics is part of **Gamepad**, not a `requiredFeatures: ['haptics']` WebXR descriptor. The older `Gamepad.hapticActuators` / `pulse()` path may be supported as a documented compatibility alias only if a coherent behavior is implemented and tested; prioritize the modern `vibrationActuator.playEffect()` and `reset()` contract. `trigger-rumble` should only be advertised if it is actually implemented and validated.

The phone profile's transient `screen` input has **no gamepad or haptic actuator**, and inline sessions receive no XR controllers.

## Context

- Work from and target `dev`, using the repository's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), and English Issue/PR templates.
- Current code: `src/polyfill/device-adapter.ts` (`ControllerInput`, `SourceGamepad`, currently null haptics), `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts` (session and source lifetimes), `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts` (emulated controller updates), `src/app/panel.ts` / `src/app/panel.html` (left/right controller visual state), `src/types/contracts.ts` and the content/background messaging path. Keep `src/devices.json` restricted to Quest 3 and Generic Android Phone.
- [Current conformance inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/webxr-conformance.md) and the [deferred haptics note on PR #20](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/20#issuecomment-6293952926) explicitly identify virtual haptics as missing because there is no actuator or panel output.
- Respect the existing same-source Gamepad identity, stable button/axis samples, permanent disconnection on source retirement and session end, and genuine cross-realm API/object allocation protections added through PRs #28, #60 and #62. No physical haptic device, extra browser permissions, unsafe privileged bridge or source spoofing is required.
- The Gamepad spec's result values `complete` and `preempted`, supported effect enumeration, visibility/liveness restrictions and parameter validation matter. Implementation must not claim true hardware timing/force fidelity; document any chosen emulated duration limits.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **Expose a functional Quest actuator:** Each active left/right tracked Quest `XRInputSource.gamepad` provides a stable `vibrationActuator` supporting at least `dual-rumble` through `playEffect(type, parameters)` and `reset()`. Advertise only supported `effects`. Preserve existing Gamepad identity, mapping, frozen/read-only input snapshots, and same-source actuator identity as frames advance. Keep unimplemented effect types unsupported, not successful no-ops.
- [ ] **Define and implement the haptic contract:** Validate/convert effect type and parameters (duration, start delay, strong/weak magnitudes) with appropriate WebIDL-compatible behavior and errors. Simulate scheduled start, independent strong/weak intensities, duration and completion. A newer effect or `reset()` stops/replaces the previous one with correct `complete`/`preempted` Promise results and no orphaned unresolved Promises. Verify zero-duration and boundary values; reject unsupported effect types, invalid values and disallowed document states as appropriate. Cap or safely handle extreme durations to avoid unbounded UI work.
- [ ] **Make requests visible in DevTools:** Display a clear **left-versus-right** haptic indicator in the real panel (strength(s), state and/or remaining duration), including delayed start, completion, replacement and reset. UI effects need not move the 3D headset, produce audio or actually vibrate. Verify the visible feedback occurs when the application calls the actuator, and is cleared when the effect finishes. Keep unrelated select/squeeze controls and 3D controller transforms functional.
- [ ] **Use a constrained bridge:** If page-side haptic state is sent to the extension's panel, define typed, allowlisted data-only messages with finite bounded values and controller/session routing. Retain the current inspected-tab/frame isolation and strict validation; page-controlled events must not invoke privileged actions, arbitrary URLs or other tabs' UI. Do not require extra permissions, external services, remote code or experimental browser flags.
- [ ] **Honor source and session lifecycle:** Left and right controllers have independent actuator states. Source removal/replacement, device or Quest mode switch, `XRSession.end()`, document hidden/pagehide, page/extension unload and restart cancel active/pending effects, clear panel indicators and settle outstanding Promises according to documented semantics. A retained disconnected Gamepad cannot revive haptics in a later session; its actuator must not affect a newer source. Genuine related-realm calls and receiver checks must not let page code forge backend actuators or reuse stale registration handles.
- [ ] **Preserve unsupported modes:** Android AR transient screen sources continue to expose `gamepad === null`; inline sessions have no XR controller haptics. Do not create or advertise a standalone `haptics` XRSession feature or require an extra feature descriptor. Handle optional legacy `hapticActuators` / `pulse()` compatibility explicitly: implement and test its documented semantics if offered, or clearly leave it unsupported.
- [ ] **Automated validation:** Add focused contract and integration tests covering API shape, supported/unsupported effects, parameters and errors, Promise resolution/preemption, timers, visibility, left/right independence, Gamepad/source identity and retirement. In actual unpacked Chromium and packaged Firefox runtime where supported by the established harness, drive both Quest VR and MR application haptic calls, confirm real panel visual feedback, and exercise end/restart, settings changes, cross-frame/tab routing and cleanup. Reuse existing tests and avoid fragile sleeps where a deterministic clock/effect state can be observed.
- [ ] **Preserve regressions:** Existing WebXR input selection/squeeze, controller tracking and dragging, hand input, Hit Test, DOM Overlay Preview, AR scene, reference spaces, WebGL presentation, and browser-extension messaging must continue working. Explicitly report any tested versus untested combinations.
- [ ] Execute and record actual results for `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, relevant focused Chromium/Firefox test commands and the applicable existing `npm run test:browser`/`npm run test:firefox` and `npm run test:samples` selections. Separate genuine passing results from skipped/unperformed checks, avoid hardware certification claims and retain relevant screenshots/reproducible observations.
- [ ] Update README and `docs/webxr-conformance.md` with the precise Gamepad API surface, Quest VR/MR coverage, the desktop visualization, a usage snippet and any intentional differences from real vibration hardware or browser-specific legacy Gamepad APIs. Include test reproduction steps.
- [ ] Submit a focused PR against `dev` with the required template, review and evidence. Close this Issue only when virtual haptic calls **actually produce observable panel feedback** and the public API's lifecycle/error/Promise behavior passes the documented acceptance tests—not merely when the property is non-null.

## Optional validation

- Add and validate the legacy `hapticActuators[0].pulse()` compatibility route only if concrete existing WebXR application consumers require it; clearly distinguish its Boolean result from modern `playEffect()` result strings.
- Exercise an unchanged public WebXR example that requests vibration on Quest controllers, if available, or add a small realistic example for future manual verification.
- Physical-controller comparison is not necessary for desktop-only simulated feedback.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All required public API, panel feedback, security and lifecycle checks are pre-merge verifiable; physical device testing and browser-store release are outside the scope of this Issue.
